liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deal** (2 reviews): Deal is the evening's highlight, with sax playing in a laid-back, rocking style; In Deal, Branford sticks to single-bar blasts, which the reviewer finds somewhat brilliant [36][37]
- **High Time** (1 review): Jerry sings High Time with weathered, wise delivery drawn from years of knowing the song [30]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Names Estimated Prophet among versions for the ages, alongside Shakedown, High Time and Franklin's Tower [27]
- **Standing On the Moon** (1 review): Reviewer hears a delicate, soulful version with Branford's sax weaving in and out [35]

## Setlist highlights

- **It Takes A Lot To Laugh It Takes A Train To Cry**: rare: 9 archived performances [39]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-09-10.dts.mtx.haugh.gems.98655.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 167 min [1]
- **gd1991-09-10.Nak300CP4.JB.Keo.117024.Flac1644**: audience recording; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Excellent recording; only flaw is slight tape warble at start of second set [2]
- **gd91-09-10.sbd.sacks.511.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 4.49/5 by 68 [5]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is top-notch; musicians' interplay and smiles come through audibly; Reviewer describes the sound quality as perfect [34][36]
- **gd1991-09-10.mtx.amdig.gems.98132.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 167 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [8]

## Around the show

- Branford walked out and tuned up before Shakedown; reviewer, attending on their birthday, didn't expect him to stay all night but he did [29]
- Reviewer was supposed to attend this as their first show but went to a party instead [31]
- Branford and Bruce are heard chasing each other musically; reviewer sees Jerry, Bruce and Branford as bandleaders [34]
- Phil's bass is especially strong throughout, and Branford fits into the band naturally [37]
- Branford Marsalis plays saxophone throughout the show [8]
- Reviewer prefers 1970s Dead and finds the 1990s less compelling, yet rates this show highly because of Branford Marsalis [27]
- Reviewer calls it one of the best shows after Brent's death that they attended [29]
- A 1960s/70s fan, whose first downloaded 80s/90s show was this one, praises the quality of the playing [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-09-10.dts.mtx.haugh.gems.98655.flac16**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: DTS 5.1 Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]. Also: Matrix recorded by James Young and Clay Brennecke using B&K 4011 mics in ORTF into Neumann preamps to DAT; Transfer from Todd Evans's DAT master via TASCAM DA-20 and LynxTWO soundcard into Wavelab 6.0; Jamie Waddell edited [1]
- **gd1991-09-10.Nak300CP4.JB.Keo.117024.Flac1644**: taped by JB; transferred by Keo;Heaton; source: Master Audience Nakamichi CM300/CP4 Shotguns>Sony D5; Recorded By JB,Transfer By Keo,Tapes From Heaton; Tapes:Maxell Metal Capsule 100,Maxell MX 110; Transfer… [2]
- **gd91-09-10.sbd.sacks.511.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD> DATs> CDRs> EAC> SHN [5]
- **gd1991-09-10.mtx.amdig.gems.98132.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dan Haugh; source: Matrix of GEMS sources (See notes) [8]. Also: Matrix mixes soundboard and audience from two GEMS sources, time-synced in CEPro 2.0, transferred by Todd Evans in January 2009 [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden](https://wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com/2021/05/grateful-dead-madison-square-garden.html) [40]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden - September 10, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/september-10-1991) [41]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 9/10/91 Madison Square Garden, New York, N…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759944723/) [42]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759944723/) [43]

claims.text: Reviewer prefers 1970s Dead and finds the 1990s less compelling, yet rates this show highly because of Branford Marsalis
Names Estimated Prophet among versions for the ages, alongside Shakedown, High Time and Franklin's Tower
Branford walked out and tuned up before Shakedown; reviewer, attending on their birthday, didn't expect him to stay all night but he did
Reviewer calls it one of the best shows after Brent's death that they attended
Jerry sings High Time with weathered, wise delivery drawn from years of knowing the song
Reviewer was supposed to attend this as their first show but went to a party instead
A 1960s/70s fan, whose first downloaded 80s/90s show was this one, praises the quality of the playing
Sound quality is top-notch; musicians' interplay and smiles come through audibly
Branford and Bruce are heard chasing each other musically; reviewer sees Jerry, Bruce and Branford as bandleaders
Reviewer hears a delicate, soulful version with Branford's sax weaving in and out
Deal is the evening's highlight, with sax playing in a laid-back, rocking style
Reviewer describes the sound quality as perfect
Phil's bass is especially strong throughout, and Branford fits into the band naturally
In Deal, Branford sticks to single-bar blasts, which the reviewer finds somewhat brilliant
Matrix recorded by James Young and Clay Brennecke using B&K 4011 mics in ORTF into Neumann preamps to DAT
Transfer from Todd Evans's DAT master via TASCAM DA-20 and LynxTWO soundcard into Wavelab 6.0; Jamie Waddell edited
Recording by JB on Nak 300CP4, from source tapes provided by Heaton
Excellent recording; only flaw is slight tape warble at start of second set
Branford Marsalis plays saxophone throughout the show
Matrix mixes soundboard and audience from two GEMS sources, time-synced in CEPro 2.0, transferred by Todd Evans in January 2009
